phase_title: Phase 4: gstack Sync and AAW Packaging Repair

findings.description: The phase plan's gstack success criteria states '✓ The upstream suite passes, with the exact command and exit code recorded.' The recorded and independently re-verified result is a failing suite: `bun run test:windows` exit=1, 7 failing tests, 3/7 shards passing. The criterion as literally worded is not met; only the honest-recording half of it is.
findings.evidence: .advanced-plans/evidence/2026-08-26-phase-4-loop-001-gstack-sync.md:117-138 records 'bun run test:windows / exit=1 / real 1m21.061s' with the shard table showing 3 PASS, 4 FAIL. Directly confirmed the cited genuine defect at C:\Users\mharvey2\Coding\aaw worktrees\gstack-sync-2026-08-26\browse\test\build.test.ts:16, which reads `expect(() => execSync(`node --check ${SERVER_NODE}`, { stdio: 'pipe' })).not.toThrow();` — an unquoted interpolation, exactly as the evidence file describes at line 172. Note for context: .advanced-plans/phases/phase-4/plan.md's own Risk Assessment table (row 'The upstream gstack suite does not run on native Windows') names this exact scenario and its accepted mitigation is 'Record the failure honestly ... do not claim a passing suite that was not run' — which is what the loop did. The mitigation covers honesty of reporting; it does not retroactively satisfy the stated pass bar.

failure_notes: The gstack upstream suite does not pass on this machine (bun run test:windows exit=1, 7 failing tests). Of the 7, 3 need `jq` on PATH, 2 need Windows Developer Mode (symlink privilege), 1 is a Git Bash fork() flake, and 1 is a genuine upstream bug (browse/test/build.test.ts:16, unquoted execSync interpolation, triggered by the space in the worktree path) that pre-dates the sync and is not fork-specific. None of the 7 is attributable to re-running loop-001; the fix requires either environment remediation (install jq, enable Developer Mode) that is outside any loop's allowed paths, or an upstream fix to gstack, or an explicit human waiver of this specific success criterion. loops_to_revert is left empty because re-running ralph-loop-001 with the same environment would reproduce the same result.

summary: Eleven of the twelve phase-4 success criteria are satisfied by direct, independently re-checked evidence: the gstack sync branch exists in gstack-fork exactly at upstream/main's head with fork main untouched (verified by reading the git refs directly), the merge-base net-patch test was used correctly, the Windows install smoke passed and left the live profile untouched, the branch carries zero AAW-specific changes, and all seven AAW-packaging criteria (tracked glue skill, fresh-clone completeness, a proven-failing packaging test, ACC-02, ACC-16, uninstall content preservation, and USERPROFILE-only global path resolution) are backed by file content read directly from the feat/aaw-packaging-repair worktree at C:\Users\mharvey2\Coding\aaw worktrees\aaw-packaging-repair. The one criterion that fails on a literal reading is 'The upstream suite passes': the recorded, independently-reproducible result is bun run test:windows exit=1 with 7 failing tests, 3 environmental (missing jq), 2 environmental (Windows Developer Mode off), 1 a Git Bash fork() flake, and 1 a genuine upstream quoting bug in browse/test/build.test.ts:16 that this review re-confirmed by reading the file directly. The phase plan's own risk register anticipated exactly this outcome and accepted honest-failure-recording as the mitigation, which the loop executed with unusual rigor (isolation re-runs, an (invalid) pre-sync control run, and an independent cross-model review that re-derived every claim) — but that mitigation covers the honesty of the report, not the literal 'passes' bar the success criterion states. This session had no shell tool available (Read/Glob/Grep/Write only), so two criteria requiring a live `git ls-files` and a live fresh `git clone` rest on direct file/gitignore inspection plus the loop's and an independent codex reviewer's own contemporaneously recorded command output, rather than a rerun performed by this review. One minor, non-blocking discrepancy: the Key Deliverables table names the idempotency-evidence file as '<date>-packaging-repair.md', but the actual idempotency content lives in '<date>-phase-4-loop-003-installation-state.md'; the substance is present under a different filename than the plan predicted. Given the one critical, high-confidence, directly-reproduced failure against a stated success criterion, the verdict is fail; the failure is narrow, fully attributed, and does not implicate the quality of the AAW packaging repair work, which is unusually thoroughly proven.
